Subject: MAP: PioneerHealth hosting lane alignment & pilot sprint

Alex / Sara — attaching our initial Mutual Action Plan (Pioneer_MAP_v1.pdf) and a short proposal for the evaluation sprint. High-level ask: confirm whether Pioneer prefers the compliance-first path (Private EU) or a hybrid pilot (Dedicated US + Private EU) so we can lock procurement and infra timelines.

Quick summary of the proposed 3-week MAP:
- Week 0: kickoff & environment access, compliance checklist completed (legal/procurement kick-in)
- Week 1: feature validation PoC on Redwood Hosted (fastest path to validate prompts/outputs)
- Week 2: Dedicated pool in US-east for load/latency testing (predictable throughput)
- Week 3: Private deployment (VPC) in EU region for PHI/PH-regulated traffic; final cutover rehearsal

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- End-to-end latency below 300ms P95 for 512-token gen in Dedicated trial
- Data residency controls validated for EU Private deployment
- SOC2/HIPAA evidence provided and reviewed by Pioneer security

Attachments: Pioneer_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft) and SOC2-2024-summary.pdf.

Asks for you: 1) which deployment lane do you want to prioritise for the pilot? 2) who is the procurement/legal contact to sign off on MAP milestones by Apr 5? 3) any hard constraints on timeline or on-prem lead time we should know about?

I can jump on a 30-min call today if that helps.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear draft. A couple of notes from Pioneer side: we have a hard requirement that any PHI-processing must remain in the EU. That pushes us toward Private deployment in the EU for production. For evaluation, though, we'd consider a staged approach if the data is synthetic or de-identified.

Questions: 
1) Can you provide the SOC2 / HIPAA attestation and a short runbook on data deletion for Private deployment? (we're copying procurement).
2) Is a hybrid approach possible: Dedicated in US for non-PHI (latency-sensitive traffic) + Private EU for PHI? We need to understand routing and failover behaviors.
3) Procurement will want a clear statement of lead times for Private (VPC/on-prem) config — anything under 2 weeks will be tough for us on the legal/process side.

Prefer to have legal & procurement sign the MAP before we lock Week 3. Could you add a line for procurement sign-off and an estimated SLA for Private?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex

PioneerHealth

Alex / Ben — copy and a technical read on feasibility and a suggested pilot structure that balances speed + compliance. Replying inline to Alex's points: 

> Can you provide the SOC2 / HIPAA attestation and a short runbook on data deletion for Private deployment?
Yes — attached SOC2-2024-summary.pdf covers the controls and we will provide a HIPAA attestation addendum. Data deletion: we support tenant-scoped retention policies and immediate key rotation + KV cache flush for a given tenant; we'll deliver a short deletion runbook in Week 0.

> Is a hybrid approach possible: Dedicated in US for non-PHI + Private EU for PHI?
Technically yes. Recommended approach: 
- Week 1 (Hosted PoC): use synthetic or scrubbed data on Hosted to validate prompts and routing rules quickly. No PHI in Hosted.
- Week 2 (Dedicated US-east): run latency/load tests with redacted production-like traffic to validate throughput and autoscale policies. This proves economic and latency parameters.
- Week 3 (Private EU): spin up Private VPC in EU for PHI traffic acceptance testing and run a DR cutover rehearsal.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Private EU provisioning (VPC + initial hardened config) typically requires 3 business days for cloud VPC + 10 business days for on-prem packaging and security review; if Pioneer needs fully air-gapped on-prem, add 3-4 weeks.
- Model choices: for low-latency interactive endpoints we'll recommend a quantized LLM variant; we should align on max seq length to size Dedicated pools correctly.
- Fallback: if Private cannot be provisioned in time, we can use a short-term Dedicated EU region variant with contractual assurances for data segregation (but legal will need to sign this).

I'll attach a pilot-architecture-diagram.png and update the MAP doc with these technical milestones. If procurement requires lead times shorter than 10 business days for Private provisioning, we need to flag that as a timeline risk in the MAP.

-Karthik
